title: Point-in-Time Discipline
concept: All fundamental and event features must use announced_at or available_at, not report period alone.
evidence: PIT literature and replication failures from look-ahead bias.
application: Enforce timestamps in data contracts and reject future observations.
validation: Re-run with delayed feature availability and compare.

title: Market Efficiency and Closing Odds
concept: Liquid markets already embed most public information.
evidence: Market efficiency and post-publication decay literature.
application: Always compare against benchmark and closing prices.
risk: Small model edge is consumed by costs.
validation: Beat benchmark after costs in multiple OOS windows.

title: Factor Investing
concept: Value, quality, momentum and low volatility are long-run candidates but regime-dependent.
application: Use risk-neutralized multi-factor scores with realistic turnover.
validation: IC, long-short spread, drawdown and capacity review.

title: Earnings Forecast Signal
concept: Positive earnings guidance can contain incremental information when published.
application: Use announcement date and event direction before changing weights.
risk: Forecast revisions, cancellations and stale news.
validation: Event-window excess return and OOS IC.

title: Shareholder Concentration
concept: A falling shareholder count can indicate concentration, but interpretation depends on price and liquidity.
application: Treat as a weak secondary feature.

title: Risk Budgeting
concept: Position size should follow risk budget, not conviction language.
evidence: Kelly, volatility targeting and drawdown-control literature.
application: Cap single-name, sector, turnover and portfolio drawdown.
validation: Stress tests and Monte Carlo drawdown paths.

title: Event Study
concept: News should be represented by entity, event type, time and expected cash-flow channel.
application: Link company/policy events to affected revenue, cost or valuation drivers.
risk: False causal mapping and prompt injection from web text.
validation: Compare event-window response against matched controls.

title: Offline Reinforcement Learning
concept: RL is more suitable for position sizing and execution than low signal-to-noise stock selection.
evidence: Offline RL and financial control literature.
application: Train action policy in simulator with transaction costs and constraints.
risk: Unsafe live exploration and reward hacking.
validation: Multiple seeds, OOS regimes and paper trading.

title: Deflated Sharpe
concept: Many trials inflate the best observed Sharpe.
evidence: Bailey and Lopez de Prado; multiple-testing research.
application: Record every trial and adjust significance.
risk: Selecting the best backtest by luck.

title: Execution Cost
concept: Turnover, spread, impact and capacity determine whether paper alpha survives.
application: Use no-trade bands, volume participation and slippage models.
